traditions.p: Late Edo period (from 1835) to present; make-up brushes from the mid-20th century
traditions.d: Hand-made brushes from Kumano for calligraphy, painting and make-up; designated a Japanese traditional craft in 1975.
traditions.tech: More than 70 mostly hand steps; hair selected and assembled, tip shaped in a wooden mould rather than cut, oil removed with rice-husk ash, bound with linen thread.
traditions.mat: Goat, horse, deer, raccoon dog, weasel and cat hair; wood and bamboo handles
ctr: Founders Tameji Sasaki (1835), Tsuneta Otomaru and Jihei Inoue (1846)
traditions.auth: Only brushes whose heads are made in Kumano by the traditional techniques may use the name (collective trademark since 2004); uncut, shaped tips.
